name: Stuffed Paratha
instructions: 1. Knead the whole wheat flour with water and a pinch of salt to form a soft, pliable dough and let it rest for 20 minutes.
2. Mix boiled potatoes with green chilies, coriander, salt, red chili powder, garam masala, and amchur to create the stuffing.
3. Take a lemon-sized ball of dough, flatten it slightly, and place a spoonful of stuffing in the center.
4. Bring the edges together to seal the stuffing inside, forming a smooth ball.
5. Dust with flour and gently roll the ball into a round paratha, being careful not to let the stuffing leak.
6. Heat a griddle (tawa) and place the paratha on it.
7. Cook on both sides, applying ghee liberally, until golden brown spots appear and the edges are crispy.
description: Stuffed Parathas, particularly the Aloo variety, are an iconic culinary emblem of Delhi, famously associated with the historic Paranthe Wali Gali in Old Delhi. It is a hearty, comfort-food breakfast typically served with a dollop of white butter, spicy green chutney, and tangy pickled vegetables.
